brief: GS's weekly macro roundup spans FX, rates, equities and research. Dollar performance stayed mixed. GS frames two tail risks for the dollar: slowing AI capex, which would be bearish dollar and bullish yen, versus resurgent European sovereign credit stress, which would be bearish EUR and bullish dollar and KRW. GS judges the credit scenario more likely, with a benign baseline pointing to low volatility and a slightly weaker dollar. The yen is framed as an improving hedge against AI-driven equity and dollar vulnerability, with GS short EUR/JPY tactically and favoring short USD/JPY longer term as a hedge against a broad AI shock. CNY continues gradual appreciation toward GS's 6.70 three-month and 6.40 twelve-month targets, helped by a record September trade surplus. TWD stays bullish medium-term despite AI-linked October outflows, alongside an upgraded Taiwan GDP forecast and a new call for a December rate-hike start. In rates, GS favors belly-of-curve long duration, Euro-area flatteners and JGB flattening. Equities Prime data show a third straight week of net selling, led by TMT de-grossing nearing July's scale, even as GS argues for buying the dip in the AI complex.
